findings.title: No per-line BDD slot; §5 matrix maps only 5 feature groups for 30+ individual lines
findings.description: C1 requires every EARS line to carry at least one BDD scenario slot via a @bdd: tag, scenario-ID placeholder, or coverage-matrix row keyed to that specific line. The §5 matrix has exactly five rows (one per PRD §9 feature). None of the ~30 individual EARS lines in §3 or the 9 lines in §4 carry an inline @bdd: tag or [BDD-pending:EARS.01.03.xxxx] placeholder. Lines entirely unrepresented at line granularity include (non-exhaustive): 5aa9, db78, 00b9, 539b, a0ae, a17e, ab5e, c7e3, ee86, fa44, fab2, d808, 0b67, 135e, a2ae, 9671, 3312, b5fa, d8a2, 86ae, 97c4, 8df7, 19ec, 187c, a132, and all nine §4 quality-attribute lines. The §5 downstream note claims 'all five P1 features, error paths, security controls, durability, and concurrency invariants mapped (PRD 100%)' but that claim is not verifiable from the matrix structure: a BDD author cannot enumerate which EARS lines require distinct scenarios without resolving the five feature rows into individual line obligations. The forward BDD pointer ('BDD-01 pending L4') is credited, but it operates at feature granularity and leaves the per-line authoring obligation implicit.
findings.recommendation: Add a [BDD-pending:EARS.01.03.xxxx] inline placeholder beneath each EARS line in §3 and §4, OR expand the §5 matrix from 5 PRD-feature rows to one row per EARS line with columns: EARS line ID | upstream PRD anchor | downstream BDD slot. Either approach closes the per-line BDD authoring obligation without requiring BDD IDs to be assigned at this layer.

findings.title: Coverage matrix lacks EARS line ID column; constraint- and risk-derived lines absent; §4 lines absent
findings.description: C2 requires bidirectionality: each EARS line mapped upstream to its PRD anchor AND downstream to an expected BDD slot. The §5 matrix columns are PRD feature | PRD | BRD | Downstream BDD — there is no EARS line ID column, so the EARS-to-PRD upstream direction is absent from the matrix structure itself (it exists only as inline @prd: tags in §3). At least 13 EARS lines derive their primary upstream anchor from PRD §12 constraints or §13 risks rather than the five §9 feature rows, and none appear in the matrix: fa44 (PRD.01.12.6f96), a2ae (PRD.01.12.19b6 / b4aa), 86ae (PRD.01.13.7760), 8df7 (PRD.01.13.ebf9), 00b9/0b67/135e (PRD.01.13.9a6d), 9671/539a/539b (PRD.01.13.0769), ee86/ab5e/b5fa/c7e3/d8a2 (PRD.01.13.835e). Additionally, all nine §4 quality-attribute EARS lines (EARS.01.04.*) are absent from the matrix entirely despite carrying formal EARS IDs and @prd/@brd references. Their downstream BDD slots are correspondingly undeclared.
findings.recommendation: Add an EARS line ID column to the §5 matrix so each row is keyed to a specific EARS line. Add rows for all constraint- and risk-derived EARS lines and all §4 quality-attribute lines, each with their upstream PRD anchor and a BDD-pending downstream slot. A separate sub-table labelled 'Constraint- and Risk-derived Lines' and another for '§4 Quality Attributes' is acceptable if keeping the feature table intact is preferred.

findings.title: Audit-log write has no idempotency declaration
findings.description: EARS.01.03.a17e requires the Metrics Reporter to write caller identity, role-decision, and timestamp to an audit log WITHIN 100 ms. This is a durable append to persistent storage. Four other stateful lines (f909, 8f70, 539a, 8df7) carry explicit idempotency parentheticals that are confirmed correct. a17e carries none. If the log write is retried after a transient failure within the 100 ms window, duplicate audit entries may be recorded; whether that is acceptable or not is undeclared. A BDD author testing audit-log correctness cannot assert a deterministic expected record count under retry conditions.
findings.recommendation: Append an idempotency note to EARS.01.03.a17e. Minimum form: '(Idempotency: each grant/deny event produces exactly one audit record; writes retried within the same request scope are deduplicated by request ID.)' If append-only duplication is acceptable by policy, state that explicitly so BDD authors know not to assert deduplication.

findings.title: Capacity-utilization alert emission has no idempotency declaration
findings.description: EARS.01.03.00b9 requires the Shortening API to emit a capacity-utilization alert to the Service Owner when the pool crosses the high-utilization threshold. Alert emission is a stateful side-effect. If the system re-evaluates the condition while still above threshold (e.g., on each incoming request), repeated identical alerts may be emitted. No edge-trigger, cooldown, or deduplication guard is declared. A BDD scenario testing alert behavior cannot assert the expected emission count without this declaration.
findings.recommendation: Add an inline idempotency or edge-trigger note, e.g.: '(Idempotency: the alert fires at most once per threshold-crossing transition; subsequent requests that remain above threshold do not re-emit the alert until utilization drops below and re-crosses, or a configured suppression window expires.)'

findings.title: Throttle and cooldown state transitions have no idempotency declarations
findings.description: EARS.01.03.ab5e (abuse detection triggers throttle + detection event) and EARS.01.03.c7e3 (enumeration-probe detection triggers cooldown + detection event) both write persistent throttle or cooldown state for a source. If the threshold is exceeded by multiple requests in close succession before the write completes, the state transition could be applied multiple times or the detection event emitted multiple times. No at-most-once or idempotent-write guard is declared for either line. The dependent IF-lines (b5fa relying on ab5e's cooldown; d8a2 relying on c7e3's cooldown) cannot be unambiguously tested without knowing the semantics of re-application.
findings.recommendation: Add an idempotency parenthetical to both lines. Minimum forms: ab5e — '(Idempotency: throttle for a source is set once per detection window; concurrent detections within the same window do not stack or emit additional events.)'; c7e3 — '(Idempotency: cooldown for a source already in cooldown resets or extends the window per configured policy; it does not stack additional cooldown periods.)'

findings.title: 'PRD 100%' coverage claim is unsubstantiated for §4 quality-attribute lines and constraint/risk-derived lines
findings.description: The §5 closing note asserts 'Coverage: all five P1 features, error paths, security controls, durability, and concurrency invariants mapped (PRD 100%).' This claim is not substantiated by the matrix structure: (a) the nine §4 quality-attribute EARS lines have no matrix row and no BDD downstream slot, (b) the ~13 constraint- and risk-derived lines in §3.4 are collapsed into the five feature rows rather than individually enumerated, and (c) 'PRD 100%' implies complete upstream PRD coverage but the matrix does not enumerate PRD §12 constraint and §13 risk anchors from which many §3.4 lines derive. A coverage auditor reading only the matrix will conclude that quality-attribute and constraint-derived requirements are untested, which contradicts the claim.
findings.recommendation: Either revise the coverage claim to 'Coverage: all five P1 §9 functional features mapped; §4 quality-attribute and §12/§13-derived lines tracked inline via @prd tags (BDD slot assignment deferred to L4)' — making the scope of the claim explicit — or substantiate '100%' by expanding the matrix to include rows for all EARS lines as described in QA-002.
